# Pattern Review: Brackenford Hall

## Input Quality and Limitations

The log covers three distinct events in one month, with one occurrence per event. E1 and E2 have supported diagnoses: technicians reproduced each fault, confirmed a damaged cable, and removed the fault through replacement. E3 has no investigation record, so its cause is unknown.

## Summary

| Candidate | Occurrences | Distinct Instances | Cause Consistency | Confidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Display interruption: E1–E3 | 3 | 3 | Same cause confirmed for E1–E2; E3 unknown | High for recurring symptoms, not a shared cause across all three |
| Damaged cable: E1–E2 | 2 | 2 | Independently confirmed in both | High within this log; only two instances |

## Genuine Patterns

Damaged cables recur across E1 and E2, two distinct events in different rooms. Independent reproduction, diagnosis and successful replacement support the same recorded cause.

No contradictory diagnosis is supplied for either event. However, the log does not establish why the cables became damaged or whether a shared upstream driver exists. Confidence is high in the repeated damaged-cable fault, not in any broader explanation.

## Misleading Surface Patterns

E1 and E2 use identical wording, while E3 describes a similar display interruption differently. Together they establish a symptom group, but not a three-event cable-fault pattern.

E3 cannot yet be classified as the same cause or a different cause. There is no confirmed misleading surface pattern involving different diagnosed causes; the risk is prematurely assigning E3 to the cable group.

## Isolated Signals, Not Yet Patterns

E3 is one undiagnosed instance of a screen going black. It is not evidence of a separate causal pattern.

## Suggested Actions for Human Approval

- Have a person check the E1 and E2 diagnoses and assess whether the repeated cable faults warrant further investigation.
- Investigate E3 before assigning it to a causal group.
- Consider checking how the two cables were damaged before approving any preventive fix or process change.

## What This Sample Cannot Tell You

This complete three-event monthly log supports a repeated damaged-cable finding in two events. It cannot establish E3’s cause, a common reason for cable damage, longer-term recurrence, or the effectiveness of any proposed preventive change.
